rungs.stem: Cu Chulainn's charioteer Loeg had two brothers, and each of the three sons of Riangabar drove the chariot of one of the three great Ulster champions -- Loeg for Cu Chulainn, one brother for Loegaire Buadach, one brother for Conall Cernach. What was the family patronymic all three shared?
choices: mac Riangabra
mac Roich
mac Ailella
mac Nessa
rungs.context: The three charioteer-brothers were Loeg mac Riangabra (with Cu Chulainn), Sedlang mac Riangabra (with Loegaire Buadach), and Id mac Riangabra (with Conall Cernach). Mac Roich is Fergus's line (Ferghus mac Roich); mac Ailella is Sencha's; mac Nessa is King Conchobar's. Source: https://timelessmyths.com/celtic/warrior-society/minor-celtic-characters/laeg/

rungs.stem: Cu Chulainn's two chariot-horses were not bought, bred, or bartered for. In the Ulster Cycle they first appeared to him as a boy, rising out of a mountain pool at the moment he first took up arms. From what did the Grey of Macha and the Black of Saingliu come up into the world?
choices: out of a mountain pool
out of a stallion of the Sidhe
out of an egg of the Morrigan
out of the sea-god's herd
rungs.context: The pool is Linn Liaith on Sliab Fuait -- a gift, the tradition says, from Macha herself (or her sister the Morrigan). The horse-of-the-sea (Enbarr) belongs to Manannan mac Lir; egg-birth is a Greek pillar motif (the Dioskouroi); stallion-of-the-Sidhe is a different Irish tale-shape. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liath_Macha_and_Dub_Sainglend

rungs.stem: When the two horses first rose from the mountain pool, the boy Cu Chulainn caught the Grey and mounted him. To break him, the tradition says, he did one very particular thing: he stayed on the horse's back through a single feat that no other Ulsterman could match. What did he do to tame the Grey?
choices: he rode the horse right around Ireland in a single day
he raced the horse the length of the Boyne against a swan
he wrestled the horse to its knees at the ford
he sang the horse to a stop with a druid's chant
rungs.answer: he rode the horse right around Ireland in a single day
rungs.context: The tradition says the horse ran the whole coast of Ireland in one day without throwing the boy, and only then submitted. After that only Cu Chulainn could handle either horse. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liath_Macha_and_Dub_Sainglend

rungs.stem: The mountain pool the two horses rose from is on a specific range in Ulster, and it is the pool the Grey of Macha will return to at the end of his life to disappear into and die. On what range of hills does the pool lie in the Ulster Cycle?
choices: Sliab Fuait
the Hill of Allen
Ben Bulben
the Boyne Valley
rungs.context: Sliab Fuait is the range of hills the medieval Irish placed in south Armagh; the Grey rose from Linn Liaith on Sliab Fuait and returned to it wounded to die. The Hill of Allen is Fionn's seat in the Fenian Cycle; Ben Bulben is where Diarmuid dies; the Boyne Valley is the Newgrange country. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liath_Macha_and_Dub_Sainglend

rungs.stem: On the morning of the fatal battle in the Aided Con Culainn, the charioteer Loeg went out as usual to yoke the chariot. But the Grey of Macha would not let him. The horse turned his left side three times against Loeg; only when Cu Chulainn himself came out did the horse consent to the harness. As the harness was being set, one further omen came from the horse himself. What did the Grey do as the harness went on?
choices: he wept tears of blood onto Cu Chulainn's feet
he tore his own bridle-rein in his teeth
he cast his own shoe into the fire
he stamped a print into the flagstones
rungs.answer: he wept tears of blood onto Cu Chulainn's feet
rungs.context: The tears-of-blood omen is one of the darkest images in the whole cycle; the Grey knows what the day will bring. Loeg had never been refused before that morning. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liath_Macha_and_Dub_Sainglend

rungs.stem: The killings at the fatal battle came in a very deliberate order. Lugaid mac Con Roi held three magical spears and each was prophesied to kill a king. His FIRST spear did not take Cu Chulainn. Whom did the first of the three prophesied spears take instead?
choices: Loeg the charioteer -- 'the king of chariot-drivers'
the Grey of Macha -- 'the king of horses'
the Black of Saingliu -- 'the king of dark runners'
Conall Cernach -- 'the king of foster-brothers'
rungs.answer: Loeg the charioteer -- 'the king of chariot-drivers'
rungs.context: The three-spear order in the Aided Con Culainn: first spear takes Loeg (king of charioteers); second spear takes the Grey of Macha (king of horses); third spear takes Cu Chulainn himself. The prophecy attached to each spear is that it will fell a king, and each does. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A1eg

rungs.stem: Loeg the charioteer was more than a driver: he carried out Otherworld errands for Cu Chulainn as well. In the tale Serglige Con Culainn ('The Sickbed of Cu Chulainn'), Loeg is sent alone into the fairy country with a strange guide to bring back a report on the woman his lord has fallen for. Who guides Loeg into the Otherworld to scout for his master?
choices: Li Ban, sister of the fairy Fand
Manannan mac Lir, sea-god of the wave
the Morrigan in her raven-shape
Cathbad the druid of Emain Macha
rungs.answer: Li Ban, sister of the fairy Fand
rungs.context: Li Ban is Fand's sister; she comes as messenger and takes Loeg into the Otherworld so he can describe Fand's country back to the bedridden Cu Chulainn. Manannan is Fand's own husband and closes the tale. The Morrigan and Cathbad are figures of a different cycle-strand. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%A1eg

rungs.stem: After Cu Chulainn was dead upon the standing stone at the ford, and Medb's warriors held off at a distance, the wounded Grey of Macha turned back from the water and charged into the mass of the enemy to defend his master's body from being looted. The tradition counts the kill in specific numbers. What tally did the horse take with teeth and hooves alone?
choices: fifty men with his teeth and thirty with each hoof
twelve men with his teeth and twelve with each hoof
ninety men in total, evenly split among his four feet
a hundred and one -- one for each of the Fianna
rungs.answer: fifty men with his teeth and thirty with each hoof
rungs.context: The horse-tally is one of the most cited numbers in all of Irish heroic corpus: fifty by tooth, thirty by each of four hooves. It is the horse, not any man, that defends the corpse. The other three counts belong to no source. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liath_Macha_and_Dub_Sainglend

rungs.stem: When the wounded Grey of Macha had finished defending the corpse, he did not just run off to die. He crossed the country to Cu Chulainn's foster-brother -- Ulster's second-greatest warrior, the one bound to take the vengeance -- and led him back to the standing stone where the body lay. Which foster-brother did the Grey lead to Cu Chulainn's body?
choices: Conall Cernach
Ferdiad mac Damain
Fergus mac Roich
Loegaire Buadach
rungs.context: Conall Cernach is Cu Chulainn's foster-brother and the vengeance-taker of the Ulster Cycle; the Grey's guiding him to the body is what sets Conall on Lugaid mac Con Roi. Ferdiad was killed by Cu Chulainn himself at the Ford; Fergus was in Connacht exile; Loegaire had fled the beheading-bargain long before. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liath_Macha_and_Dub_Sainglend

rungs.stem: The Grey of Macha's name binds him to a specific Ulster goddess whose curse -- laid on the Ulstermen after they had forced her to race a chariot while pregnant -- laid every man of the province flat with the pangs of childbirth for nine generations. Cu Chulainn was the only Ulsterman spared the pangs, and the horse he rode carried her name. Who was the goddess?
choices: Macha
the Morrigan
Danu
Brigid
rungs.context: Macha is the horse-goddess whose curse falls on the Ulstermen -- 'Liath Macha' is 'the Grey of Macha' and binds Cu Chulainn's mount to her. The Morrigan is the war-goddess in raven-form who lands on Cu Chulainn's shoulder at the end. Danu is the eponymous mother of the Tuatha De Danann. Brigid is the goddess of fire and healing at Kildare. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macha
